minutes.headline: Commission ordered sand moved off a Townsend Harbor Road lake slope and approved a small sand patch at the top
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission endorsed a stormwater committee's letter for a 319 grant application, then worked through a run of wetlands hearings, continuing several and issuing negative determinations or orders of conditions on others. The longest discussion was a contested sandy beach at 307 Townsend Harbor Road. A lake management update on fanwort control followed, along with agent reports.

public_comment.topic: Stormwater committee member asked the Commission to endorse a letter supporting a 319 grant application for stormwater work at the Mulpus Brook headwaters, due June 1.
Resident suggested a compacted base material instead of sand for the beach at 307 Townsend Harbor Road, noting long recreational use of the spot.
Another resident said the beach area has been used for generations and is where debris collects.
Abutter raised concerns about the proposed driveway, trees and notice to Hickory Hills for the 141 Hemlock hearing.

Approve minutes of April 4th with changes.

what_happened.line: The Commission voted to update the 307 Townsend Harbor Road permit so sand is moved to a small patch at the top of the hill and removed by June first.
It issued negative determinations for Horizon Island Road, Highland Street, Fire Road and 435 Townsend Harbor Road, and a standard order of conditions for 54 Maple Parkway and 179 Island Road.
Hearings for Hickory Hills, 455 Mass Ave, 352 Townsend Harbor Road, 141 Hemlock and 564 Page Street were continued, mostly to June 6.
The Commission was recorded taking up a vote to endorse the stormwater committee's letter for a 319 grant application; the outcome is not audible in the captions.
An enforcement order for 164 Page Street is to be delivered by constable, with a fine to be considered at the next meeting.

why_it_matters: Decisions on shoreline sand, tree removal and building near wetlands set what abutters and lake users can do at the water's edge, and the sand ruling affects a spot residents say has long been used for recreation.

The 319 grant would bring state money toward stormwater work at the Mulpus Brook headwaters, with the committee covering the remainder including in-kind contributions, so its fate shapes what the town itself must contribute.
watch_next: June 6 continuations for 141 Hemlock, 564 Page Street, 455 Mass Ave and 352 Townsend Harbor Road.
The next meeting, where a fine for the 164 Page Street enforcement order is to be considered.
